title: What’s Next: Wi-Fi 8
summary: IEEE 802.11bn is being written now, with reliability as its goal.

beats.heading: The next amendment is in development
beats.body:
The IEEE is already working on the next generation: P802.11bn, "Enhancements for [[uhr|Ultra High Reliability]]", which is expected to become Wi-Fi 8. It is still in development and has not been approved {{wifi8-status}}.

Everything on this tab is forward-looking and subject to change.
beats.bottomLine: Wi-Fi 8 is not a reason to wait: Wi-Fi 7 is the current, certified generation, and Wi-Fi 8 is expected to build on it.
beats.sceneDescription: The generation timeline continues past Wi-Fi 7. A new pillar for Wi-Fi 8 appears at the end, drawn only as a dashed violet outline and labelled as in development, because the standard is not finished.

beats.heading: From faster to more reliable
beats.body:
Where Wi-Fi 7 focused on throughput and lower [[latency|latency]], the stated goal of 802.11bn is reliability: fewer lost messages and more consistent performance, including with interference and movement {{wifi8-reliability-def}}.

The project's goals include at least 25% more throughput than Wi-Fi 7 in at least one mode {{wifi8-throughput-goal}} and 25% lower latency for the slowest 5% of messages {{wifi8-latency-goal}}.
beats.bottomLine: The next generation targets exactly the problems that matter most in clinical settings: dependable delivery, not just speed.
beats.deepDive: The P802.11bn PAR defines reliability improvements in terms of throughput, latency and MPDU loss {{wifi8-reliability-def}}, with targets of at least 25% higher throughput {{wifi8-throughput-goal}} and 25% lower 95th-percentile latency {{wifi8-latency-goal}} than 802.11be in at least one mode. These are project goals, not measured results; the technical mechanisms are still being decided in task group TGbn {{wifi8-status}}.
beats.sceneDescription: A link from an access point to a device passes through bursts of interference. In the Wi-Fi 7 colour it occasionally flickers; in the dashed Wi-Fi 8 outline it is shown holding steady, illustrating the reliability goal rather than any measured result.

beats.heading: What to do today
beats.body:
Deploy Wi-Fi 7 where it solves today's problems, and make choices that carry forward: [[multigig|multi-gigabit]] switching, sufficient [[poe|PoE]] budgets, 6 GHz-capable designs and clinical devices with current Wi-Fi support.

We will update this page as 802.11bn progresses {{wifi8-status}}.
beats.bottomLine: Investments in wired infrastructure and 6 GHz design for Wi-Fi 7 are expected to carry forward to the next generation.
beats.sceneDescription: The Wi-Fi 7 pillar glows steadily while the dashed Wi-Fi 8 outline beside it gently pulses, suggesting a path forward that builds on today's generation.
